Lead one of the most ambitious global transformation programmes in the VELUX Group and help shape the future of customer engagement across our business. With your strong programme leadership experience and ability to bridge business and technology, you will play a key role in delivering a global CRM platform that enables better customer experiences, stronger commercial performance, and lasting business value.

Meet your future team

You will join our global Sales Enablement & Strategic Pricing organisation and work closely with colleagues across Sales, Marketing, Customer Service, Finance, and IT & Digital Excellence. In this highly visible role, you will collaborate with senior leaders, project teams, business stakeholders, and external partners across the VELUX Group.

You will report to the VP Sales Enablement & Strategic Pricing, with a dotted reporting line to the VP IT & Digital Excellence, Sales & Marketing.

As Global CRM Program Lead, you will be accountable for driving our global CRM transformation programme from strategy through implementation and business adoption. You will act as the connecting link between commercial ambitions, technology delivery, and organisational change, ensuring alignment across markets while creating value for the business.

What We Offer

This is an opportunity to take ownership of a strategically important global programme and influence how the VELUX Group engages with customers for years to come. You will be given significant responsibility, engage with senior stakeholders across the organisation, and lead a complex transformation that reaches across functions and geographies.

More specifically, your tasks will be to:

• Define and drive the overall CRM programme strategy, roadmap, governance, and delivery approach.

• Ensure alignment between business objectives, technology solutions, and value realisation across all markets.

• Lead executive stakeholder management, steering committees, and programme decision-making.

• Manage programme scope, budget, risks, dependencies, and benefits realisation.

• Oversee implementation partners and ensure high-quality delivery of CRM solutions, integrations, and data migration activities.

• Drive global rollout planning, market readiness, adoption, and change management activities.

• Build strong collaboration across Sales, Marketing, Customer Service, Finance, and IT functions.

What You Will Bring

You are an experienced programme leader who thrives in complex, international environments and can successfully navigate the space between strategy and execution. You combine strong commercial understanding with technology insight and know how to bring people together around a common goal.

Moreover, we expect that you:

• Hold a Master's degree in Business Administration, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field.

• Have extensive experience leading large-scale CRM or enterprise transformation programmes in global organisations.

• Have a proven track record of delivering complex cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, markets, and external partners.

• Understand commercial processes within Sales, Marketing, and Customer Service and how technology can enable business value.

• Bring strong financial and business acumen, including experience managing programme budgets and business cases.

• Have experience working with CRM platforms such as Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, or similar solutions.

• Excel at stakeholder management and are confident engaging with senior leaders and executives.

• Bring programme or project management certifications such as PgMP, PMP, PRINCE2, MSP, or SAFe, which will be considered an advantage.

• Are a collaborative and resilient leader who creates alignment, drives decisions, and delivers results.

Learn more about the VELUX Group online at www.velux.com where you can read more about working at our company and what to expect of our recruitment process.

We look forward to receiving your application and CV as soon as possible. We are conducting interviews on an ongoing basis until we have the right match.

In the VELUX Group, we offer you a world of opportunities and the chance to create a bright future. From the forefront of the roof window category, we enable those who live, work and play under the roof transform their spaces and live a healthier everyday life with more daylight and fresh air.

The VELUX Group is an international, family-owned business with strong financial roots and each year we can create real impact by reinvesting in society, our employees and planet through our foundations. jobs.occupation: Postdoc in RNA function and gene regulation
jobs.description:
The laboratory of Ulf Vang Ørom is inviting applications for a 2-year postdoctoral position at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics at Aarhus University.

The position will focus on RNA and its role in regulating cellular pathways relevant for metabolic processes.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2–year position from February 1 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter with possibility for extension of the employment.

Job description
You will be working using several methods to study RNA, protein-interactions and epigenetics, often including high through-put methods. The project focuses on novel aspects linking RNA, metabolism and epigenetics, and allows for active involvement in shaping the project within its duration. You will be working with a high degree of independence and in collaboration with other researchers at the institute and internationally.

Your profile
Applicants should have a PhD degree in a relevant area and expertise with working with RNA and high through-put methods.

Applicant should have a high-quality publication record and excellent language (English) skills.

Who we are
The Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics (https://mbg.au.dk/en/) hosts researchers in the areas of RNA and protein biology, bioinformatics and nutrition, as well as plant research, giving great opportunities for interdisciplinary collaborations.

What we offer 
The department offers

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Universitetsbyen 81, 8000 Aarhus, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments. 

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Ulf Vang Ørom, PhD, +45 22288766

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 30 November 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc Positions in Natural Language Processing (CPH)
jobs.description:
The Department of Computer Science at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for two or more postdoc positions in the area of Natural Language Processing (NLP). The positions are open for appointments from January 1, 2027 or soon thereafter. The duration of the positions is one or two years, depending on the candidate’s qualifications and preferences. The positions are at AAU’s Copenhagen campus, located at the waterfront in Sydhavnen.

The application deadline is Monday, November 9, 2026. Interviews are tentatively planned for December 10, 2026.

The positions are hosted within the Natural Language Processing (NLP) research group https://aaunlp.github.io/ at AAU Copenhagen, and postdocs will work under the academic leadership of Professor Johannes Bjerva https://bjerva.github.io/. The NLP group is a rapidly expanding research environment with strong activities in multilingual NLP, LLM security, linguistically informed approaches to NLP, factuality in LLMs, and socially sustainable AI. The group is supported by several major national and international research grants – in 2026, we have grown to 20 researchers, including a full professor, four assistant professors, one postdoc, two research assistants, and 12 PhD students.

As a postdoc, you will join a highly collaborative, international, and ambitious research community, with access to state-of-the-art computational resources. In your role, you will have the opportunity to develop an independent research profile and compete for individual fellowships and faculty positions. The positions include the opportunity to undertake one or more research stays abroad to facilitate knowledge exchange with top research environments worldwide. The positions are in part funded by a DFF: Sapere Aude project (“Building TRUST in Text: Linguistically Motivated Language Model Detection”) Building TRUST in Text: Linguistically Motivated Language Model Detection - Aalborg University's Research Portal, an NNF: Ascending Data Science Investigator project (“LM2-SEC: Linguistically Motivated Language Model Security”)  https://vbn.aau.dk/en/projects/linguistically-motivated-language-model-security/, and an Erasmus+ project on AI-based Personal Language Learning Assistants in collaboration with VSKDansk  https://www.brondby.dk/om-kommunen/nyheder/2025/08/vskdansk-far-eu-stotte-til-udvikling-af-ai-baseret-sprogtutor.

Your work tasks

As a postdoc, you will conduct research within the area of multilingual NLP. We are seeking postdocs with two distinct profiles within this area:

• Postdoc 1: Security, Safety, and Privacy in Natural Language Processing and AI, with a focus on Large Language Models (LLMs), LLM-based systems, and Agentic AI

• Postdoc 2: AI-based personal language learning assistants (1 year) and AI security (1 year).

Furthermore, there will be the possibility to gain experience as a co-supervisor for PhD students associated with these projects, and to supervise students on BSc. and MSc. levels.

The positions are embedded in an active and rapidly growing research environment, including ongoing projects on, e.g., AI security, epistemic diversity, linguistically motivated NLP, and knowledge-graph grounded factuality in LLMs. The postdocs will work both independently and collaboratively within the group and will have opportunities to engage with national and international partners. As a part of the projects funding these positions, we will host internationally recognised researchers at AAU, creating additional opportunities for collaboration and knowledge exchange.

Your competencies

We are looking for candidates motivated to make fundamental scientific contributions to multilingual NLP and AI security. Candidates should have the ambition of reaching an internationally leading level of research excellence by building their own research profile, while contributing to the research environment.

Applicants must have:

• A relevant PhD degree (e.g., NLP, AI, ML, Security, Cryptography, or a related field) and a relevant MSc degree (e.g., Computer Science, Software Engineering, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Computational Linguistics, or a related field)

• Strong skills in machine learning and deep learning

• Extensive experience with modern ML and NLP methods, including experience with experimentation, and with publishing in top-tier venues (e.g. ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS, ACL, EMNLP, TACL)

• Excellent communication skills in English

Applicants with documented experience in security, privacy, safety, or robustness will be preferred.

**Qualification requirements

**Appointment as postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

Who we are

According to the most recent US News and World Ranking, Aalborg University ranks 4th in Europe and 27th in the world within Best Universities for Engineering. According to a 2018 MIT report, Aalborg University is considered to have the 4th best engineering program in the world. According to the recent Times Higher Education Impact ranking, Aalborg University ranks 9th in the World for UN SDG Impact.

The Department of Computer Science at Aalborg University is highly regarded among researchers, students, and external partners because of our leading research, education, and collaboration. The department currently has more than 170 scientific staff, 20 administrative staff, and 1,100 students. Education and research are built around AAU's problem-based learning model.

The Section for Copenhagen at the department is a highly collaborative research environment, currently expanding from around 40 employees to approximately 60 over the next few years. The section includes members from research groups within NLP, AI, ML, Databases, Formal Methods, Human-Centred Computing, and others, and is uniquely characterised by an open, friendly, and supportive atmosphere. Daily life in the section is marked by informal interactions, knowledge sharing, and a strong sense of community. We also host a bi-weekly SemiBar (a combined seminar and Friday bar), where staff are challenged to present their research in a manner that provokes discussion across our diverse scientific backgrounds, along with regular social events, reading groups, cross-group research activities, and a newly established local PhD organisation promoting an active social and scientific life among our most junior researchers. Together, these initiatives create a dynamic and welcoming environment for early-career researchers and senior staff alike.

The Natural Language Processing (NLP) group, led by Professor Johannes Bjerva, is a rapidly expanding research environment specialising in multilingual NLP, LLM security, linguistically informed AI, and trustworthy language technologies. The group hosts several major research projects funded by, e.g., the Carlsberg Foundation, Danmarks Frie Forskningsfond (DFF), the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and AAU’s AI:X initiative. The group collaborates broadly across Europe and globally, and offers an inclusive, ambitious, and supportive research culture.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Cover letter, stating your motivations for applying and your qualifications in relation to the position – at most one page.

- Please indicate your preferred starting date, and your preferred duration of employment (at least 1 year, and at most 2 years).

- We ask applicants not to use generative AI or writing assistant tools in the preparation of their cover letter, except for basic grammatical and spelling correction.

• Curriculum Vitae (CV) - at most two pages

• A full list of publications.

- For three of these publications, include a single brief paragraph detailing your contributions to the work.

• Diplomas (bachelor, master's, and PhD degree diplomas)

• Project description – at most two pages.

• Please describe your research vision for the position in relation to the project topics outlined above.

• Other relevant document

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

VP of Quantum - Diasense ApS

Reports to: Marvin Holten, Founder and CTO

Team: Quantum Lead, Quantum Engineers, and part-time specialists in quantum information science and quantum optics, growing through 2027

Location: Quantum Denmark, Copenhagen, Denmark. On-site.

Start: January 2027

Company Overview

Diasense is a deep-tech company turning fundamental quantum physics into world-class scientific instruments. We are building the world's most sensitive magnetic microscope, using nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond to measure magnetic fields at a sensitivity that no other technique can reach.

We are applying that instrument to one of the hardest measurement problems in semiconductor manufacturing: seeing what is actually happening inside a finished chip, electrically and non-destructively. It is a market where the physics has to be exceptional and the engineering has to be industrial, and very few companies in the world are attempting both.

We are a spin-out of DTU Physics, based in the quantum center of Copenhagen, and we are about to move from a working prototype to instruments installed at customers’ sites. The team today is eight full-time and six part-time people. Over 2027 and 2028, we are building that to around thirty. By joining now, you will be one of the people who decide what this company becomes, not someone who inherits it.

Position Overview

Job Description

We are looking for the person who will own the quantum side of our instrument, outright.

You will lead our quantum function: a Quantum Lead, quantum engineers, and part-time specialists, growing over the next eighteen months. You are an experimentalist at heart. We are not looking for someone who manages a lab from a desk. We are looking for the person other physicists go to when something does not work, and nobody can say why. Today that person is our CTO, and your role is to change that. When the quantum work gets stuck, it should stop with you.

You will be joining at the transition point where the instrument moves from lab to customer sites. The physics has to keep improving, and it now also has to withstand contact with the real world. Both halves of that are yours.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Ownership of the Quantum Platform

• 
Own the performance of the NV-diamond measurement chain end to end: optical read-out, microwave control, sensitivity, noise floor and measurement protocols.

• 
Set the technical direction for how we push sensitivity and measurement speed over the next two years.

• 
Make the calls on where the physics effort goes, and be accountable for them.

Hands-on Experimental Work

• 
Spend the majority of your week in the lab, on the instrument, with your hands on it.

• 
Diagnose and fix the problems that have no procedure attached - the ones where the measurement is wrong and nobody yet knows why.

• 
Develop and prove new experimental protocols, rather than reviewing someone else's.

Leading and Building the Quantum Team

• 
Lead the quantum function: our Quantum Lead, quantum engineers and part-time academic specialists, with further hires planned through 2027.

• 
Raise what the team can do unaided. Success looks like fewer problems reaching you over time, not more.

• 
Own hiring for the quantum team as it grows, together with the CTO.

Instruments in the Field

• 
Take technical responsibility for the quantum performance of instruments installed at customer sites.

• 
Support and eventually supervise measurement campaigns at customer locations, so that deployment does not depend on the founders.

• 
Work closely with instrumentation, software and applications colleagues - this instrument only works when all four disciplines agree.

Qualifications & Experience

• 
A PhD in Physics, Quantum Optics, Atomic Physics or a closely related field, followed by substantial further experimental experience in academia or industry.

• 
Deep, sustained, hands-on experimental physics. Years at the bench, building and debugging experiments yourself. This is the single most important qualification and we will test for it.

• 
A demonstrable record of solving unfamiliar, hard experimental problems without supervision. We are interested in what you did when the standard approach failed.

• 
Experience guiding, mentoring or leading other researchers or engineers - formally or informally. You do not need to have held a management title, but you do need to want this half of the job.

• 
An inquisitive and stubborn mindset: willing to question assumptions, including your own, and to keep going after a problem that has already resisted three attempts.

• 
Fluency in Python or MATLAB for research-grade data analysis.

Experience with one or more of the following is a significant advantage:

• 
Cold atoms or trapped ions. Our techniques originate in cold-atom physics rather than in quantum sensing, and we have found that people trained in that tradition tend to carry exactly the debugging instinct this role needs.

• 
Magnetometry, especially with NV centres, and precision measurements.

• 
Microwave electronics and real-time control systems.

• 
Building complex free-space optical systems from components.

• 
Taking a laboratory technique out of the laboratory.

Compensation & Benefits

A competitive salary package.

• 
An attractive warrant package. You will share directly in what you build, and at this stage the share is meaningful.

• 
Relocation support for you and your family, and assistance with the Danish researcher tax scheme, which for qualifying international hires taxes salary at a flat 32.84 percent for up to seven years.

Denmark's quantum ecosystem at your door: DTU Physics, the Niels Bohr Institute and one of Europe's densest concentrations of quantum research.

A small, senior team where decisions are made in a conversation rather than in a process.

USP's for this job

• 
You are the ceiling, not waiting for one. In most companies, the deepest technical authority sits above you, and you work within it. Here you are being hired to become it. The quantum direction of this instrument will be yours.

• 
Lead a team without leaving the lab. Almost every physicist who moves into leadership loses the bench. This role is explicitly designed so that you do not - the leadership comes from being the best experimentalist, not from stopping being one.

Build the Unprecedented: You will be a leading the development and rollout of the most powerful magnetic microscope in the world, directly pushing the boundaries of scientific measurement.

Early enough to matter. Fourteen people today, around thirty by the end of 2028. The people joining now set how this company works.

Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC), University of Copenhagen

   

  BRIC wishes to recruit a strongly motivated scientist at Associate Professor or Professor level for an independent research group leader position. We are seeking excellent candidates with ambitious research visions within translational diabetes type 1 or 2 research and a drive to contribute to a diverse and inspiring research environment. The research group leader position is combined with a senior researcher position at the Bartholin Institute, Department of Pathology, Centre for Diagnostics, Rigshospitalet, Capital Region. The start date is 1 April 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

In order to be considered, the applicant must send two applications: one to the faculty (the research group leader position) and one to the hospital (the senior researcher position) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the senior researcher position. This also applies to applicants who are already employed at the Hospital. The advertisement for the senior researcher position is available here

  The workplace
 BRIC is an international center of excellence with the mission to perform cutting-edge basic and translational biomedical research in an open environment that fosters interdisciplinarity and collaboration. Active research areas include many aspects of cancer biology, stem cell biology and neurobiology. The center is part of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. 

  Job description
 As a group leader, you will establish an independent research program within translational diabetes research. Your capacity to integrate research and clinical perspectives is emphasized. In the job, you will be expected to:

   	
• Conduct, publish, and communicate high-quality research that moves the field forward 	
• Engage in outreach and knowledge-sharing with society 	
• Develop your research group through attraction of competitive funding and talent development of team members 	
• Conduct research-based teaching and examination 	
• Be involved in academic assessments 	
• Be involved in local as well as international collaborative and multidisciplinary research projects and engage in core center activities such as talent or technology development to advance BRIC’s research environment and culture   You are also expected to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills and to contribute to developing the research environment and culture at BRIC.

  50 % of the working time is employment at Copenhagen University and will be allocated to academic tasks (e.g., research, teaching, evaluation tasks and communication with the public) in agreement with the Director at the Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC). The remaining time will be allocated for other tasks at the Bartholin Institute and the Department of Pathology (e.g. research administration, personnel responsibility, methods establishment and development, grant writing and the establishment of a competitive research group) in agreement with the Head of the Bartholin Institute.

  Candidate profile
 Your background includes a PhD degree, postdoctoral training, and a track record documenting your research experience as reflected in a strong publication record matching your career stage. Also desired is a successful record of attraction of funds, leadership and educational experiences, collaboration experiences and additional capabilities within areas such as outreach or technology transfer activities, again reflecting your career stage.  

  We offer

   	
• Access to cutting edge technologies through core facilities, including high-content screening, flow cytometry, next-gen sequencing, bioinformatics, microscopy, single cell genomics, histology and access to spatial transcriptomics and pathology services. Additional core facilities are available at faculty level. 	
• A vibrant and open scientific community with focus on collegiality, collaboration and creativity.  	
• A focus on talent training and development at all career stages, including strong PhD and postdoc programs. 	
• Strategic support for funding strategizing, grant writing and implementation of larger grants and collaborations and for research communication and outreach. 	
• A package covering the salary of 1-2 group members and technical support equivalent to 50 % of a full-time technical position from the Bartholin Institute. 	
• Administrative support with regards to laboratory services and safety, purchase, economy, HR, and IT. 	
• Additional start support may be obtained from private foundations (obtained at individual or center level).   Terms of employment
 Initial appointment as group leader (Associate Professor) is for 6 years.

  BRIC wants to offer a further career path pending a positive evaluation following transparent guidelines, which include the UCPH criteria for recognizing merit

  This can happen in form of employment in a permanent position based on public advertisement, or the group leader may enter the University of Copenhagen Promotion Program towards a position as full professor (permanent position). Experienced research leaders may be recruited at the level of full professor. 

  The average weekly working hours in the combined position are 37 hours per week.

  Salary and other terms and conditions of appointment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations. 

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

  Additional information about BRIC can be found on www.bric.ku.dk

  Inquiries are welcome to Director Anders H. Lund bric-director@bric.ku.dk

  Recruitment process
 The recruitment process will contain four evaluation steps: 

   	
• After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager will shortlist applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointment Committee after an evaluation of the written application material. Evaluation criteria can be seen here. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. Due to differences in career stage or institutional background, not all candidates are required to fulfil all requirements in full. 	
• The Vice Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. The selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee, and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. 	
• Selected candidates will be evaluated in an online interview with the Appointment committee. The online interviews is expected to be carried out between late January and early February  	
• Selected candidates will be invited for an on-site visit and final evaluation in late February    

  To be qualified for a Professor or Associate Professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion..

  You can read about the recruitment process here: Recruitment process  – University of Copenhagen.

• Cover letter outlining the applicant’s motivation to apply to BRIC and brief summaries of research visions (1 page).

• Research vision/goal and synergy with BRIC 		
• Current and future research plan 		
• Description of five most significant contributions (e.g., scientific, clinical, commercial achievements, honours/awards)

Consultant Interventional Cardiologist – PCI On-Call Service

Department of Cardiology, Aalborg University Hospital, Denmark

The opportunity
Are you an experienced interventional cardiologist looking to join a highly specialised university hospital with a strong clinical, academic and collaborative environment?

The Department of Cardiology at Aalborg University Hospital is seeking one or more Consultant Interventional Cardiologists from the EU/EØS to join our team. We welcome applications from candidates who are already qualified to participate in a PCI on-call service, as well as experienced PCI operators who are motivated to develop the additional competencies required for on-call duties.

The position is available as soon as possible or by mutual agreement.

This is an opportunity to work in a busy interventional cardiology environment, contribute to the development of specialised cardiac care and collaborate with highly skilled colleagues across cardiology, cardiac surgery and other disciplines.

The position
Your primary clinical responsibilities will be within interventional cardiology, particularly percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
The position includes participation in the department's PCI on-call service.

You will be part of a multidisciplinary team providing specialised care for patients with ischaemic heart disease, including patients requiring urgent and complex coronary interventions.
Depending on your experience, qualifications and the department's clinical needs, there may also be opportunities to contribute to the development of other specialised interventional services, including transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and chronic total occlusion (CTO) procedures.

Alongside your clinical responsibilities, you will contribute to the department's research, teaching and professional development activities, as well as relevant administrative and organisational tasks.

What we offer

• The opportunity to work in a busy university hospital with an established PCI service and a broad range of specialised cardiology services.
• Professional development: Opportunities to further develop your interventional skills and, where appropriate, expand your expertise into complex PCI, TAVI or CTO procedures.
• A strong multidisciplinary team: Close collaboration with cardiologists across subspecialties, cardiothoracic anaesthetists and cardiac surgeons.
• An academic environment: Opportunities to participate in clinical research, teaching and the development of new treatment pathways.
• Supportive colleagues and leadership: We value professional respect, constructive collaboration and a positive working environment.
• Flexible working arrangements: Working hours and duty schedules are organised within the applicable employment framework.
• An international perspective: The opportunity to join a university hospital committed to clinical excellence, research, education and continuous improvement.
Qualifications and experience
Essential requirements

• You hold specialist certification in cardiology.
• You have or are able to obtain a Danish Authorization to practice medicine
• You are fluent in or command a professional working proficiency in Danish. Norwegian or Swedish (B2/C1 level)
• Or are willing to learn Danish
• You can perform PCI procedures independently.
• You have the clinical judgement and professional skills required to manage patients with ischaemic heart disease.
• You communicate effectively and work constructively with colleagues across clinical disciplines.
• You can maintain an overview and make sound clinical decisions in a demanding and sometimes unpredictable environment.
• You are committed to high standards of patient care, patient safety and continuous professional development.
• You are willing to contribute to the department's clinical, organisational and educational activities and to take on the leadership and supervisory responsibilities associated with a consultant position.
Desirable qualifications

• Experience participating in a PCI on-call service.
• Experience from a university hospital or another highly specialised cardiac centre.
• Experience in complex PCI, TAVI or CTO procedures.
• A PhD, or other research qualifications or a strong record of scientific publications.
• Experience in clinical research, teaching or quality improvement.
• Experience in a PCI on-call service is an advantage but is not essential, provided you are an independent PCI operator and are motivated to acquire the necessary competencies following an appropriate period of training and induction.
About the Department
The Department of Cardiology at Aalborg University Hospital is a large, specialised and research-active department providing advanced care across a broad range of cardiovascular conditions, including ischaemic heart disease, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, valvular heart disease, thoracic aortic aneurysms, pericardial diseases, thromboembolic disorders and dyslipidaemia.

Our department performs approximately:

• 6,000 invasive procedures annually
• 8,000 inpatient admissions annually
• More than 30,000 outpatient consultations annually
• Approximately 14,000 echocardiographic examinations annually
Our medical team comprises doctors at different stages of postgraduate training and 32 consultant cardiologists, including two professors.
We provide inpatient and outpatient services, operate a cardiac catheterisation laboratory and maintain a dedicated cardiology research unit.
Our work is guided by a shared commitment to clinical excellence, patient safety and involving patients and their families in shared decision-making. We also have a strong responsibility for undergraduate medical education and postgraduate specialist training.
The department operates across three hospital sites in Aalborg, Thisted and Hobro, with the vast majority of clinical activity based at the newly built Aalborg University Hospital.

Salary and terms of employment
This is a full-time position. Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with the applicable Danish collective agreement.
The position includes participation in the department's PCI on-call service.
Further details regarding the on-call arrangement and employment conditions can be discussed with the Head of Department or Lead Senior Physician Bent Raungaard tlf. 27201096, e-mail: b.raungaard@rn.dk
 
Application
Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and interviews will be arranged continuously. The advertisement will be withdrawn once the position has been filled.
Please submit your application by email to:
Ljubica Vukelic Andersen
Head of Department of Cardiology
Aalborg University Hospital, Denmark
Email: ljubica.andersen@rn.dk
Telephone: +45 30 38 25 10

Please include:

• Curriculum Vitae (CV).
• Letter of motivation
• Proof of specialist certification in cardiology.
• List of publications, if applicable.
The assessment process will follow the applicable Danish requirements for consultant appointments, including assessment of competencies across the seven physician roles.
